title: Crack a walnut: push a hand nutcracker's two handles together from both sides, then bowl the kernel and plate the shell
instruction: Crack the walnut with the nutcracker: push its two handles toward each other, one hand on each, until the jaws crack the shell. Then put the kernel in the white bowl and both shell halves on the blue saucer, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Cracking nuts, crushing garlic or working pliers or crimpers all need two opposing forces on a hand tool; a light tool on a smooth worktop just slides away from a push on one handle, so the second hand is what closes it.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A steel hand nutcracker, 320 g, lying flat on a smooth worktop, its pivot 44 cm forward on the centre line. Its two levers open in a V toward the arms, 30 degrees each side of the centre line, held open by a spring against a stop; each runs 20 cm straight out from the pivot, then bends into a 9 cm red PVC handle grip that runs along the centre line. Its jaws are toothed steel blocks near the pivot. (2) A walnut, 3.5 cm across, on the worktop between the jaws, 6 cm out from the pivot. (3) A white porcelain bowl, 10 cm across and 4 cm deep, 27 cm forward and 25 cm right of the centre line. (4) A blue porcelain saucer, 12.4 cm across, 27 cm forward and 25 cm left of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Cracked: at some point the jaws closed to 2.9 cm apart where the walnut sits (it is 3.5 cm across), with the walnut between them (3.5-9 cm out from the pivot, within 1.2 cm of the V's middle line, on the worktop); the shell then breaks into a kernel and two shell halves. Judged at the end: 1.0 when it cracked, the kernel is in the bowl (its middle within 4.2 cm of the bowl's middle, inside it), both shell halves are on the saucer (each within 5.6 cm of its middle, on it) and both arms are back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5 when it cracked and the kernel is in the bowl; 0.25 when it cracked; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the kernel, the shell halves, the bowl and the saucer still.
reset_notes: A whole walnut between the open jaws; bowl and saucer empty.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the walnut is rigid and the jaws touch a 2.4 cm core inside it; once they close to 2.9 cm where it sits, the task file swaps it for a kernel and two shell halves laid along the V. The levers turn on a hinge whose spring (0.04 N m per degree) holds them open. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
